heroLead: Kimbolton sits along the National Road in Guernsey County, in coal country that transitioned into one of Ohio's busiest Utica drilling corridors.
intro: Kimbolton is a small village in Guernsey County along U.S. Route 40, in an area whose economy leaned on coal mining for generations before Utica/Point Pleasant drilling arrived in the early 2010s. Guernsey County sits within the core of the play, and mineral ownership around Kimbolton frequently traces back to coal-era severances layered under farm deeds, creating title histories that take some careful tracing to sort out.

sections.heading: Guernsey County core positioning near Kimbolton
paragraphs: Guernsey County has seen real Utica development since the play's early years, with operators including names like Antero Resources and Gulfport Energy having drilled in the broader area historically. A tract near Kimbolton may already sit inside a producing spacing unit, which means royalty statements or a recorded lease are often the fastest way to establish real value rather than a general county estimate.

sections.heading: Coal-era severances and what they mean for oil and gas rights
paragraphs: Because coal mining shaped this part of Guernsey County for so long, many original deeds separated coal from oil and gas entirely, sometimes leaving them with different owners. A title search through the Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge is how you confirm which minerals your family's specific reservation actually covers and whether the chain of title has stayed clear across the generations.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Kimbolton?
faqs.answer: Guernsey County sits within the Utica core, and tracts near Kimbolton have seen real development activity, though results vary depending on the specific spacing unit.

faqs.question: Could my family's oil and gas rights have been severed separately from coal rights?
faqs.answer: That's common in this part of Guernsey County. The original severance deed will specify exactly what was reserved and to which party.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before a valuation conversation?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together establish your net mineral acres and current decimal interest.

faqs.question: How do I know if my lease is still being held by production?
faqs.answer: Check whether a well on your pooled unit is still actively producing and generating royalty payments. If not, the lease may have lapsed under its own terms, which a title search can confirm.

faqs.question: What if my deed only reserves a fraction, not a specific number of acres?
faqs.answer: Multiply your fraction by the tract's total acreage for an estimate, though a title search through the Guernsey County Recorder confirms the figure against the full chain of title.
